Returns your company's interviews, newest first; with `updated_since`, the ones that
changed since, oldest change first. A full page comes with a `Link` header to the next one

post.description:
Makes an interview from a job description, as the key's creator would. Its questions take
a few minutes: until `ready` is true, it can't take candidates; the `interview.ready` web
hook event says when it is. Retrying is safe: the same request from the same key within 15
minutes returns the interview the first one made, with `200`.

Needs the `interviews:create` permission.

post.description:
Invites the candidate to the interview on behalf of the key's creator and reserves credits
for them, with their name if given. By default prepza emails the invitation and the
candidate signs in with that email; with `sign_in` false, your platform sends them to the
response's `invite_url`, which opens the interview without signing in. With a `return_url`,
the finished page takes the candidate back to your platform. Retrying is safe: inviting an
address whose invite is still open, or who already finished, returns that candidate as they
are (`200`), without another email or credits; an expired invite is sent again. To send an
open invite again, use the resend endpoint.

Needs the `candidates:invite` permission.

delete.description:
Withdraws an invite the candidate hasn't used yet: its link stops working and its credits
come back. A candidate who started is erased for good, with their answers and results, for
example when they ask to have their data deleted; one who answered at least one question is
charged. Your web hooks get `candidate.removed`.

Needs the `candidates:delete` permission.

get.description:
Every member sees the keys (never the keys themselves) and web hooks; only owners and
admins their whole addresses.

patch.description: Owners and admins replace a key's permissions, adding or taking away any.

put.description:
Owners and admins limit a key to the addresses its servers call from, or let it be used
from any (an empty list).

post.description:
Owners and admins give a web hook a new signing secret, shown once; the old one keeps
signing too for a day, so its receiver can switch over.
Owners and admins send a signed test event to a web hook, now.

CandidateEvent.description:
The `data` object of a candidate's event (`candidate.finished`, `candidate.started`,
`candidate.undelivered`, `candidate.expired`): the interview and the candidate as they are
when it's sent.

name.title: Name
name.description: The candidate's name, optional (at most 200 characters). It fills a name not known yet; inviting the same address again doesn't change a known one

return_url.title: Return Url
return_url.description: Where to take the candidate once they've finished, optional: any https address (http only on `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`, while you test). The finished page shows a button to it, with `prepza_invite=<candidate id>` added to its query

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: The theme the candidate's pages show, in your company's colors for it: `light` or `dark` always shows that theme, `default` the candidate's own. A `theme` added to the `invite_url` (`?theme=dark`) or given to the SDK wins over it

sign_in.title: Sign In
sign_in.description: Whether the candidate signs in to prepza with this email, which prepza sends the invitation and its reminder to. Set it to false when your platform already knows who the candidate is and sends them to the response's `invite_url` itself: the link then opens the interview without signing in, and prepza sends no emails. Anyone with that link can take the interview, so give it only to the candidate
